subject: Error working with Actiwatch derived csv files

messages.author: 36e95958feca7fb5
messages.subject: Error working with Actiwatch derived csv files
parts:
Hi all. I'm using GGIR to  reanalyze data from a previous study which was recorded with the Actiwatch Spectrum Plus. After exporting the individual files with the epoch-by-epoch activity counts on Actiware, and after getting rid of the headers (I could not get them to run at all if I didn't do this before), I have been able to process almost all of them.

However, I am running into an error with a number of files, which recordings seem to be well enough looking at them on Actiware. The error comes up in part 4 and reads:

Error in if (defaultGuiderOnset >= 24) { : argument is of length zero

Right now I detected the failing files and removed them in order to complete the process of all the others in the set, but, I wonder if I could be able to recover the failing files, considering the recordings look good enough.

Any help or suggestion will be deeply appreciated. 
Here's one of the failing files, for testing purposes:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Ypi_dQUgRmZP2ZIh0PVdYQiqtT3ljeOh/view?usp=sharing

Thanks!

messages.author: e0169f921473cc94
messages.subject: Re: Error working with Actiwatch derived csv files
parts:
I noted your failing file crosses the period in which daylight saving time (DST) ended in many parts of the world in 2018 (mid-October to early November). Do your other failing files intersect with DST starts or ends? GGIR has an internal function to identify DST nights (https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/LK8G_5dRRpM). 

I received the same error you mentioned when I ran your file through a GGIR function that I have used on other Actiwatch CSV files. On a lark I changed the months in your example file to May, June, and July, then tried the code again. It ran to completion!

I further tested your original file with an additional parameter, desiredtz = "Asia/Seoul". South Korea does not observe DST. The code ran to completion.

Hopefully a GGIR developer can take a closer look and confirm/refute whether the error you're receiving is in fact related to DST!

messages.author: 36e95958feca7fb5
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error working with Actiwatch derived csv files
parts:
Hi Vincent,
The data was collected in Argentina, but I have been running the code in the US. At first I didn't even set a time zone, and frankly I didn't even think of it as these csv files already have a clock time column. After Michael's comment, I set the time zone to Argentina and the code run well. I'm guessing the time zone was being detected from the computer (pacific) and used for analyzing the files. I will try to reproduce the error so I can provide better info on this kind of error.


However, this makes me think about my work with other files. I recently run a set of CWA files from AX3 devices, which hold recordings also from Argentina. I didn't indicate a time zone for these files either - I wonder if the time zone is embedded in the cwa files or not. I will rerun these files and see if the output is different or not.

messages.author: e0169f921473cc94
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Error working with Actiwatch derived csv files
parts:
I tested with Leandro's file a bit further. My data directory only contains his test file, TO06_16-Oct-18_0_01_00_New_Analysis.csv.

GGIR 3.1.2 and R 4.4.1 on Windows 11.

The following (no desiredtz set) doesn't work - it breaks at Part 4 with "Error in if (defaultGuiderOnset >= 24) { : argument is of length zero":

GGIR(datadir = datadir,
     outputdir = outputdir,
     dataFormat = "actiwatch_csv",
     do.anglez = FALSE,
     do.enmo = FALSE,
     do.zcy = TRUE,
     extEpochData_timeformat = "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M:%S",
     HASIB.algo = "Sadeh1994",
     windowsizes = c(60, 60, 3600),
     def.noc.sleep = c()
)

Setting desiredtz = "America/New_York" (my current timezone) still fails, as expected. Setting desiredtz = "Europe/Brussels" also fails.

Setting desiredtz = "Asia/Seoul" or desiredtz = "America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires" allows the code to run to completion.

That's as far as I got. Thanks for looking, Vincent!

Thanks for checking Mike.

I then conclude that it is not a bug but a matter of correctly specifying the desiredtz parameter when processing data outside the timezone where the data was collected (same for parameter configtz if device was configured in a different timezone).

It is up to the user to reflect on what GGIR parameters mean and choose them wisely.

Best,
Vincent
